answer: Each identity stakes 70 credits under a key-bound opal seal on one crystal. At a random hour every holder is called to the gale corridor: in one ten-minute window each must present the crystal at two gates and sign with its key. Auditors scan the opal seal and check serials against the roll; late, duplicate, or unsigned crystals burn the bond. First 36; the kth 36+7(k-1), the 1000th 7029; 1000 fakes 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-presenter ring fails: one body cannot sign two keys at once, and a lent key lets the hire drain the bond. An honest agent pays 36 once and keeps the bond.
